narr: A very moist and marginally unstable airmass ahead of a deep upper-level low over the lower Mississippi Valley resulted one report of a tree down and several flash flooding reports over middle Georgia. Heavy rainfall amounts of 1.5 to 3 inches were observed along a line from Thomaston to Gray to Eatonton to Comer, with pockets of higher amounts between 4 and 8 inches.
ev: The Emergency Manager reported closures of Central Road and Browns Chapel Road due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate that 2 to 5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported flooding of Reids Road from Little Glady Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 1.5 to 3 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported road closures along and near Interstate 16 near Danville. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported the closure of Sewell Road bridge over the Little River near Bowden Lake. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported the Enterprise Road Bridge over Little Sugar Creek was damaged due to high water. Radar estimates indicate that 2.5 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

Georgia DOT reported the bridge on GA Highway 22 was closed due to flooding from Ulcohatchee Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
Emergency Manager reported floodwaters affected several buildings in the Culloden area. Radar estimates indicate that 4 to 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported Treadwell Road closed in Russellville due to flooding. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported a portion of Wheeler Road was washed out due to high flow from Walnut Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported the Highway 44 bridge was closed due to high water on Big Cedar Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 4 to 8 inches of rain occurred over the Big Cedar Creek basin, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported a small wooden bridge was washed out on Jackson Road due to highwater on Shoal Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 4 to 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported the Union Hill Church Road bridge was washed out, likely due to high water on Cedar Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 4.5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

Law Enforcement reported Greene Settlement Road closed due to flooding of Little Chehaw Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 4.5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported US Highway 80E flooded near Salem Church. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported water flowing over Allen Road from Auchumpkee Creek closed the roadway. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported two culvert washouts along Pleasant Grove Road resulted in its closing between Kendall Road and Logtown Road. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Mt Carmel Road was closed due to flooding from Wrights Church Creek. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 8 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported Bentley Road closed between Kendall Road and Logtown Road due to flash flooding along Kendall Branch. Radar estimates indicate that 3 to 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
